title: every card sits where its task really is: the captain's lane means a card is pending, a chosen effect is carried out, a vanished crewman leaves the deck, the captain can set aside any unfinished task, and a wrong final state can be reopened
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-26 the captain asked why the board held so many stale cards. firstmate traced each class to a rule in board/server.ts. (a) `STAGE` maps `decision_requested` to the captain's lane, but nothing maps `decision_made`. So once a card is answered, the task stays in the captain's lane until some other event moves it. Examples: T-030 was answered B = park (D-1020, events.jsonl line 1406) and still sat in the captain's lane, never parked; the same holds for T-060 and T-064. (b) An answer is only recorded (`outcome: recorded`). An effect the card offered (park, drop, send back, dispatch) is never carried out, and nothing says it was not. (c) Crew stay aboard until `agent_finished`. A run that was killed, or whose machine slept, stays on deck, and a worker the log last saw crashing keeps its task in a lane. (d) `ACTIONS` lets the captain park or drop only untouched work (ready, backlog, parked). A task in working, gate, review or the captain's lane cannot be set aside from the board at all, although the captain must be able to order that directly. (e) `FINAL = {merged, closed}` is irreversible, and there is no event to correct it. On 2026-09-26 09:33Z a merge card for PR #96, the revert of T-105, was raised under T-117, and fm-merge wrote `merged` for T-117 (events.jsonl line 3947). T-117 has shown as merged ever since, although its own PR #97 is open, and nothing can put it back. The captain approved fixing card-state confusion on 2026-09-26. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-118.json, is committed on this branch.

The captain's lane means a pending card, and nothing else. Derive it directly: a task is in the captain's lane exactly while a card for it is pending (the existing `awaiting` set), and otherwise sits wherever its other events put it. Remove `decision_requested` from `STAGE` rather than mapping `decision_made`, so no event can leave a task stranded there. Test T-030's real sequence (decision_requested, decision_made B), a merge card answered B (hold), and a task whose card is withdrawn: none stays in the captain's lane once no card is pending.

Decisions carry out their effects, or say why not. Every card kind whose options name an effect (`effect` in the details: park, drop, merge, send back, dispatch, hold, and any other the code defines) has that effect carried out when the captain picks it, by the one script that owns it (fm-emit for park/drop, fm-merge for merge, and so on). The board also records the outcome on the decision_made event: `done`, `failed` with the reason, or `recorded` for an option that has no effect. A chosen park or drop therefore produces the `parked` or `closed` event. A card whose effect failed shows as failed on the board, with the reason, and is not silently treated as done. List every card kind and effect in design.md. Test each effect end to end with its script stubbed as the real one answers.

Crew liveness, from what already exists. Do not add a heartbeat. fm-herdr.py already asks Herdr for a pane's process (`pane process-info`). Use that, or the run's recorded pid, when the board or the existing reconcile step reads the deck: a run whose process is gone and that never said agent_finished gets one `agent_lost` event, emitted by the launcher side through fm-emit, never the model. It then leaves the deck and shows once in the log, in en and zh-TW, and its task goes where its events put it (blocked unless something later moved it). Test a vanished pid or pane, a live one, and agent_finished arriving after lost.

The captain can set aside any unfinished task. Park and drop are offered in every lane except merged and closed, with a confirm step for any task that has crew aboard or an open PR. Dropping or parking a task in flight stops its crew through the existing stop path (`fm.sh stop <task>`, from T-107 if merged, else the path that exists on main), so no round keeps working on a set-aside task. The PR is left open; the card says so, and nothing closes it without the captain. Unpark returns the task to the lane its events give it. POST /tasks refuses anything else. Update ACTIONS and the page. If T-122 has merged when this branch is rebased, the route keeps its credential check.

Reopening a wrong final state. Prevention belongs to T-119 (a merge card must match its PR's task), so no general correction mechanism is needed. Add one captain-only event, `reopened`, with `data.reason`. It is the only event that moves a task out of merged or closed, and afterwards the task's lane is derived from its later events, or from `untouched` rules if there are none. The board offers it behind a confirm step on merged and closed cards. Pending cards of a task in merged or closed are shown, not hidden, with a note that the task is final. Test T-117's exact sequence (events 3945–3947): after `reopened`, T-117 leaves merged, and a later merge card for #97 is shown and answerable.

No standing sweep. Correct derivation makes the old inconsistencies impossible, and fm-sync-prs already brings GitHub's state in. Instead, a one-time repair: `fm-reconcile.sh --repair-cards` (dry run by default, `--apply` emits through fm-emit) finds and fixes the log's existing damage: T-030/T-060/T-064-style answered cards whose chosen park or drop never happened, and T-117's false merge (via `reopened`). Its output lists each fix in en and zh-TW. Test it against a fixture copy of those events. Do not add a daily run, and do not add more checks.

Tests, each fail-first against main, and the board's e2e (Playwright) shows: an answered card's task leaving the captain's lane, a park carried out from a card, park/drop with confirm on a working card, and `reopened` moving a merged card out of merged. Stubs of outside tools answer as those tools do. Workers do not run the suite themselves: evidence is the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. design.md gets a section on lane derivation that lists every event, the lane it gives, the precedence (pending card, reopened, final, liveness), and the card effects.
